tasks.focus: Map the architecture, trust boundaries, user roles, entry points, security controls and existing tests. Read executable code rather than relying on documentation. Identify the highest-risk surfaces for follow-up review.

Review authentication, authorization, session handling, role transitions, tenant isolation and account recovery. When live tools are enabled, exercise safe synthetic login and access-denial scenarios and bind every result to live evidence.

Review backend and API behavior, validation, ownership checks, error handling, concurrency boundaries and external integrations. Use browser-visible behavior when live tools are enabled; identify additional API scenarios that still need a dedicated API client.

Review web and mobile clients, navigation guards, state handling, empty and error states, accessibility-sensitive paths and client/server contract mismatches. When enabled, run real Chromium and Android emulator/device scenarios and cite their live evidence references.
Review data classification, logging, retention, deletion, consent, export, secret handling and third-party data flows. Flag claims that require legal or runtime confirmation.

Cross-check every handoff against source and live evidence, reconcile contradictions, rank issues by evidence and impact, and produce a concrete isolated regression plan. Keep live results, source observations, suspected issues and unexecuted tests clearly separated.
